refutedOnReview: REFUTED as a shared-map claim. The sources all exist and most quotes are accurate, but the load-bearing inference fails and two stated facts are wrong.  WHAT CHECKED OUT - SpaceX enterprise-api README exists and contains the endpoint sentence verbatim: "The Starlink router hosts the server at port `9000`. The default subnet for the Starlink router is `192.168.1.1/24`, so the default gRPC server address is `192.168.1.
gotchas: Rated community-single on purpose, and it should not be built on without a bench check. The call numbers 3004/3006 are agreed across three dumps, but every field inside WifiGetStatusResponse was read from a single repository. That is a weaker footing than the dish dialect and is a different fact from 'the router answer

The router is a second device on a second subnet, not a second view of the dish. It sits at 192.168.1.1:9000 while the dish is at 192.168.100.1:9200, and cabin-starlink talks only to the dish. Nothing here reuses the dish dialect's driver.
In bypass mode the Starlink router is out of the path entirely and this endpoint is gone, while the dish at 192.168.100.1:9200 remains. Anything built on the router is the more fragile of the two.

On a Mini the router is co-housed with the terminal (HardwareIndex ROUTER_MINI_COHOUSED_1/2, ROUTER_MINI_1), so whether it answers on a separate address at all is unverified. Do not assume 192.168.1.1:9000 on a Mini.

The one vendor-documented call this endpoint serves is GetDiagnostics — see the starlink-device-diagnostics dialect, which covers the router explicitly and returns per-network client counts. If you only need 'how many things are on the WiFi', use that one and inherit its vendor-doc confidence instead of this dialect's.
unmappedReports: Connected client counts and the WifiClient list (3000) — who is on the WiFi. Unit::Count exists; no MetricKind does., Per-band radio state: rf_2ghz_status (1008), rf_5ghz_status (1009) — WifiBandStatus sub-messages., WifiAlerts (1010)., dish_disablement_code (1031) — the router's copy of the terminal's service-disablement reason. Same gap as the dish dialect., poe_stats (1022), dhcp_servers (1019), hops_from_controller (1034), captive_portal_enabled (1), is_aviation (1011)., ipv4_wan_address (1003), ipv6_wan_addresses (1017), secs_since_last_public_ipv4_change (1030) — WAN addressing and how recently it changed. Metadata, but the change timer is the kind of thing an intermittent link makes interesting., Three separate ping paths — router-to-x (1004/1005), dish (1012/1013), PoP (1014/1015), plus IPv6 PoP (1027/1029) and 5-minute averages (1018/1020/1021/1028). link-latency and link-signal-quality are single-valued, so a driver has to pick one hop and discard the rest — and picking the wrong one hides where the link actually broke.
